texts.preamble: M.Ashraf vs The State Of Kerala on 13 January, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Wednesday, The 13Th Day Of January 2016/23Rd Pousha, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 3156 of 2006 ( ) --------------------------------- Crl.A 152/2001 of Addl.Sessins Court (Adhoc)-Iv, Thiruvananthapuram Cc 477/1995 of J.M.F.C.-Ii,Nedumangad Revision Petitioners/Appellants/Accused No. 1 And 2: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1. M.Ashraf, S/O.Muhamed Hanif, Vadakkuvila Veedu, Thevanpara, Thalicode. 2. A.Illias, S/O.Abusali, Thevanpara, Thadatharikathu Veedu, Tholicode P.O. By Adv. Sri.K.M.Firoz Respondents/Complainants: -------------------------------------------- 1. The State Of Kerala, Represented By The Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala Ernakulam. 2. K.Sekharan, Food Inspector, Tholicode Panchayath, Nedumangad Circle, Nedumangad Po Thiruvananthapuram. R1 & R2 By Public Prosecutor, Shri.R.Githesh This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 13-01-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: M.Ashraf vs The State Of Kerala on 13 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169713651/ 1 B.Sudheendra Kumar, J. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - -- - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - Crl.R.P. texts.facts: Nedumangad filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16(1) (a)(i) read with Section 2(ia)(f) and 7(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 5, Appendix B.A. 05.08 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 18.8.1995 at about 12 noon, PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 450 gram of coriander whole from the shop of the second accused. The first accused was the salesman and the third accused was the person who supplied the food item to the shop of the second accused. After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P9 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for coriander whole under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1956 and therefore, the same was adulterated. It was further reported that the sample contained insect to the extent of 20% and hence the same was unfit for human consumption. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW5 were examined and Exts. P1 to P19 were marked for the prosecution. DW1 to DW7 were examined and Exts.D1 to D6 were marked for the revision petitioners.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P9 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P9 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) M.Ashraf vs The State Of Kerala on 13 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169713651/ 2 that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused. The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
